---
name: Drizzle foreign-key identifier drift
description: PostgreSQL identifier truncation can make repeated Drizzle pushes recreate long foreign keys
---

New schema foreign keys should use explicit names shorter than PostgreSQL's 63-character identifier limit.

**Why:** Drizzle's autogenerated names can be truncated by PostgreSQL while the schema serializer continues expecting the longer name. A later push then repeatedly drops and recreates the same constraint, and a full-project push can expose unrelated baseline drift.

**How to apply:** Name foreign keys explicitly in new additive schema files. For isolated proof batches, compare only the batch schema plus the project's existing enum/sequence declarations; do not let a full-index baseline drift alter certified tables.
